DORADO-001.title: Initial GPU Basecalling
DORADO-001.objective: Test whether Dorado can basecall D1 on the GTX 1060 and record an initial CUDA performance baseline.
DORADO-001.observation: All 59 reads were processed. The recorded interval covers basecalling.
DORADO-001.limitations: The 59-read input and single measurement limit conclusions about sustained throughput. The original timing logs and complete environment are unavailable.

DORADO-002.title: Ryzen 5 CPU Basecalling Baseline
DORADO-002.objective: Run the same D1 input and HAC model on the Ryzen 5 1500X CPU to establish a baseline for the GTX 1060 comparison.
DORADO-002.observation: The CPU processed all 59 reads. Its reported basecalling interval was about 79 times as long as the GTX 1060 interval.
DORADO-002.limitations: This was one run on a 59-read input. The original timing logs and complete environment are unavailable.

DORADO-003.title: RTX 4070 CUDA Baseline
DORADO-003.objective: Measure HAC basecalling on the RTX 4070 without modified-base inference.
DORADO-003.observation: The full command took approximately 12 s. The shorter basecalling interval excludes part of that runtime. Dorado selected the batch and chunk sizes automatically.
DORADO-003.limitations: One 59-read run with automatic tuning gives no sustained rate. The original timing boundaries and environment are incomplete.

DORADO-004.title: RTX 4070 Modified-Base Calling
DORADO-004.objective: Measure the stage overhead of adding the 5mCG/5hmCG companion model to the RTX 4070 HAC configuration.
DORADO-004.observation: The reported basecalling stage took 0.115 s longer than DORADO-003. Peak memory was not measured.
DORADO-004.limitations: The result is from one 59-read run. Effective tuning settings and BAM tag verification are incomplete. Modified-base accuracy was not measured.
DORADO-004.output_check: BAM MM/ML tags were reported. Tag presence and correctness remain unverified.

DORADO-005.title: Apple M2 Metal Basecalling
DORADO-005.objective: Measure D1 basecalling on Apple M2 Metal and inspect the resulting BAM.
DORADO-005.observation: The output statistics include predicted Q-scores and read lengths. Predicted Q-scores do not measure reference-aligned accuracy.
DORADO-005.limitations: The 59-read single run cannot establish sustained throughput. The scope of the reported 4.1 GB memory peak is unverified.

DORADO-006.title: RTX 3070 Mobile CUDA Baseline
DORADO-006.objective: Record a preliminary D1 basecalling rate for the RTX 3070 Mobile.
DORADO-006.observation: The short reported basecalling interval exceeded the theoretical 5 kHz input rate.
DORADO-006.limitations: The original command and run date are unavailable. Earlier reports use conflicting experiment IDs for this measurement. The 59-read run does not establish sustained throughput.

BLITZ-003.title: Initial Ryzen 7 5700U Thread Scaling
BLITZ-003.objective: Compare full-command runtime and output consistency at one and four caller threads.
BLITZ-003.observation: Four threads reduced the mean runtime.
BLITZ-003.limitations: The first, slower run was retained. Warm-up conditions and the later exact memory-measurement commands are unknown.
BLITZ-003.output_check: Read IDs, sequences, and qualities matched across thread settings.

BLITZ-004.title: Ryzen 7 7800X3D Single-Thread Baseline
BLITZ-004.objective: Measure full-command runtime and FASTQ repeatability for one caller thread on D4.
BLITZ-004.observation: Full-command runtime averaged 15.01 s across three runs.
BLITZ-004.limitations: Warm-up conditions, exact invocation, and original run artifacts are unavailable.
BLITZ-004.output_check: The three FASTQ outputs reportedly matched byte for byte.

BLITZ-005.title: Ryzen 7 7800X3D CPU Thread Sweep
BLITZ-005.objective: Measure D4 throughput, runtime variability, and peak host memory as caller threads increase.
BLITZ-005.observation: Eight caller threads gave a 5.21× speedup over one thread.
BLITZ-005.limitations: D4 is a small recorded fixture. Cache state and the exact invocation are unverified. The rates do not measure live streaming.
BLITZ-005.output_check: All 12 runs matched by read ID, sequence, and quality.

BLITZ-006.title: CPU-Package Energy on Repeated D4
BLITZ-006.objective: Measure CPU-package energy for 30 invocations of the D4 workload at eight caller threads.
BLITZ-006.observation: The session processed 271,003,620 samples by repeating the same 48 reads. Recorded energy covers the CPU package.
BLITZ-006.limitations: The 30 invocations belong to one power capture. Independent session variability and total system energy were not measured.
BLITZ-006.output_check: Output consistency was reported. Original files and checksums are unavailable.

BLITZ-007.title: Eight-Thread Performance on D5
BLITZ-007.objective: Measure full-command runtime and memory on a larger recorded workload at eight caller threads.
BLITZ-007.observation: The reported 4,092,013 samples/s corresponds to 199.81% of the 4 kHz full-channel reference and 159.84% of the 5 kHz reference.
BLITZ-007.limitations: The run used recorded files. Live latency and queue behavior were not measured. The exact basecalling command and original timing logs are incomplete.
BLITZ-007.output_check: All three runs reportedly produced matching FASTQ output.

BLITZ-008.title: CPU-Package Energy on D5
BLITZ-008.objective: Measure CPU-package energy for one full D5 pass at eight caller threads.
BLITZ-008.observation: The power session processed the 4,467-read D5 workload. Its duration and throughput come from that session.
BLITZ-008.limitations: One power session does not establish energy variability. The electrical boundary excludes other system loads.
BLITZ-008.output_check: Output consistency was reported. Original files and checksums are unavailable.

BLITZ-009.title: Jetson TX2 ARM64 CPU Baseline
BLITZ-009.objective: Measure full-command throughput and module-input energy across four caller-thread settings on the ARM64 port.
BLITZ-009.observation: The eight-thread rate of 214,574 samples/s reached 10.48% of the theoretical 2,048,000 samples/s full-channel reference at 4 kHz. The four-thread rate was close at 207,860 samples/s.
BLITZ-009.limitations: The INA3221 scale remains unverified, so watt and joule values are provisional. Memory, clock and thermal state were not recorded. The exact port build and output check artifacts are unavailable.

BLITZ-010.title: Reference Accuracy of Saved D5 Output
BLITZ-010.objective: Score the retained BLITZ-007 run-1 FASTQ against the pinned D5 reference.
BLITZ-010.observation: The saved alignment fields were verified from the per-read CSV. All 4,467 read IDs match the two saved SoCall outputs.
BLITZ-010.limitations: This was retrospective scoring of BLITZ-007 run 1. The original FASTQ was not independently re-hashed or realigned. Primary local identity excludes unaligned sequence and covers one isolate.
BLITZ-010.timing: Reference alignment of the saved BLITZ-007 run-1 FASTQ.

SOCALL-001.title: Apple M2 D5 Accuracy with Greedy Decoding
SOCALL-001.objective: Measure reference-aligned read identity and profile the SoCall greedy-decoder configuration on D5.
SOCALL-001.observation: The single profiled run used greedy CTC and per-read median/MAD normalization. The alignment summary includes unmapped reads in the mapping denominator.
SOCALL-001.limitations: The run had no warm-up. Timing is for profiling. Accuracy covers one isolate and primary read alignments.
SOCALL-001.timing: In-process stage profiling with GPU synchronization at stage boundaries.

SOCALL-002.title: Apple M2 D5 Accuracy with Beam Search
SOCALL-002.objective: Measure reference-aligned read identity and profile the SoCall beam-width-5 configuration on D5.
SOCALL-002.observation: This run used beam search with width 5 and per-read median/MAD normalization. The alignment summary includes unmapped reads in the mapping denominator.
SOCALL-002.limitations: The run had no warm-up. Timing is for profiling. Accuracy covers one isolate and primary read alignments.
SOCALL-002.timing: In-process stage profiling with GPU synchronization at stage boundaries.

SOCALL-003.title: Jetson TX2 CUDA with 300-Sample Overlap
SOCALL-003.objective: Profile SoCall FP32 throughput with 300-sample overlap and measure TX2 module-input power.
SOCALL-003.observation: Inference and greedy decoding accounted for most of the timed interval. The power capture spans both process runs, including setup and warm-up.
SOCALL-003.limitations: The INA3221 scale was uncalibrated. D1 chemistry and sampling differ from SoCall training conditions and D1 lacks a reference. The power window differs from timed processing.
SOCALL-003.output_check: A well-formed FASTQ was verified for all 59 reads on the first timed pass.
SOCALL-003.timing: Timed processing passes with CUDA synchronization at stage boundaries. Model and NPZ loading were excluded.

SOCALL-004.title: Jetson TX2 CUDA Baseline without Overlap
SOCALL-004.objective: Measure SoCall FP32 throughput across four repeated process runs and record module-input power for the final run.
SOCALL-004.observation: The reported rate was 24.8% of the 4 kHz full-channel reference and 19.9% of the 5 kHz reference.
SOCALL-004.limitations: Power was captured only for repetition 4, including setup and warm-up. The INA3221 scale was uncalibrated. D1 lacks compatible reference-scored accuracy and the runs used one board with no thermal-stability criterion.
SOCALL-004.output_check: All 59 reads produced well-formed FASTQ, byte-identical across four repetitions.
SOCALL-004.timing: Timed processing passes with CUDA synchronization at stage boundaries. Model and NPZ loading were excluded.

SOCALL-005.title: Jetson TX2 CPU Five-Read Baseline
SOCALL-005.objective: Measure the SoCall FP32 CPU pipeline on the first five D1 reads and record module-input power.
SOCALL-005.observation: Inference accounted for 99.8% of the timed interval. The CPU used PyTorch default threading. A full-D1 attempt was abandoned in warm-up.
SOCALL-005.limitations: The single measured pass uses a five-read subset. The INA3221 scale was uncalibrated and the power capture includes setup and warm-up. No reference-based accuracy was measured.
SOCALL-005.output_check: Well-formed FASTQ was verified for five reads.
SOCALL-005.timing: Timed processing pass over the first five D1 reads. Model and NPZ loading were excluded.

SOCALL-006.title: Jetson TX2 Same-Session Baseline Control
SOCALL-006.objective: Repeat the SOCALL-004 configuration in the same session as the decoder variants, so their speed-ups are measured against an unchanged baseline.
SOCALL-006.observation: Throughput matched SOCALL-004 within 0.4% and greedy decoding again took about as long as inference (48% of wall time each). The FASTQ was byte-identical to SOCALL-004.
SOCALL-006.limitations: D1 is out of distribution for SoCall, so no accuracy is claimed. Power is gross module input over each process run, including setup and warm-up, with an uncalibrated INA3221 scale.
SOCALL-006.output_check: Byte-identical FASTQ to SOCALL-004 in all three process runs.
SOCALL-006.timing: Timed processing passes with CUDA synchronization at stage boundaries. Model and NPZ loading were excluded.

SOCALL-007.title: Jetson TX2 Vectorised CPU Greedy Decode
SOCALL-007.objective: Measure throughput when greedy CTC decoding is vectorised with numpy on the ARM CPU instead of looping per base in Python.
SOCALL-007.decode: vectorised numpy on the CPU, float32 quality math
SOCALL-007.observation: Throughput rose 1.85× over the same-session baseline. Decoding fell to under 3% of wall time, leaving inference as about 90%. Sequences matched the baseline exactly, but float32 quality arithmetic moved 2 of 1,434,692 quality characters by one Phred step.
SOCALL-007.limitations: D1 is out of distribution for SoCall, so no accuracy is claimed. Power is gross module input over each process run, including setup and warm-up, with an uncalibrated INA3221 scale.
SOCALL-007.output_check: Same sequences as SOCALL-004; quality strings differ at 2 positions (float32 log10).
SOCALL-007.timing: Timed processing passes with CUDA synchronization at stage boundaries. Model and NPZ loading were excluded.

SOCALL-008.title: Jetson TX2 GPU-Side Greedy Decode (float32 Quality)
SOCALL-008.objective: Measure throughput when argmax and maximum log-probability are computed on the GPU and only labels and maxima are copied back.
SOCALL-008.decode: argmax on the GPU, vectorised collapse, float32 quality math
SOCALL-008.observation: Throughput rose 1.91× over the same-session baseline, the fastest of the first three variants, with the same 2-character quality difference as SOCALL-007.
SOCALL-008.limitations: D1 is out of distribution for SoCall, so no accuracy is claimed. Power is gross module input over each process run, including setup and warm-up, with an uncalibrated INA3221 scale.
SOCALL-008.output_check: Same sequences as SOCALL-004; quality strings differ at 2 positions (float32 log10).
SOCALL-008.timing: Timed processing passes with CUDA synchronization at stage boundaries; the GPU argmax is counted as decode time. Model and NPZ loading were excluded.

SOCALL-009.title: Jetson TX2 Exact Vectorised Greedy Decode
SOCALL-009.objective: Measure an exact vectorised replacement for the Python greedy decoder that keeps the original float64 quality arithmetic.
SOCALL-009.decode: vectorised numpy on the CPU, float64 quality math (launcher)
SOCALL-009.observation: Throughput rose 1.86× over the same-session baseline with byte-identical output, so the speed-up costs nothing in sequence or quality.
SOCALL-009.limitations: D1 is out of distribution for SoCall, so no accuracy is claimed. Power is gross module input over each process run, including setup and warm-up, with an uncalibrated INA3221 scale.
SOCALL-009.output_check: Byte-identical FASTQ to SOCALL-004 in all three process runs.
SOCALL-009.timing: Timed processing passes with CUDA synchronization at stage boundaries. Model and NPZ loading were excluded.

SOCALL-010.title: Jetson TX2 Exact GPU-Side Greedy Decode
SOCALL-010.objective: Measure the GPU-side greedy decoder after its quality arithmetic was moved to float64.
SOCALL-010.decode: argmax on the GPU, vectorised collapse, float64 quality math
SOCALL-010.observation: Throughput was 1.90× the same-session baseline with byte-identical output: the fastest exact decoder measured, adopted as the default for later TX2 runs. Inference is now about 92% of wall time.
SOCALL-010.limitations: D1 is out of distribution for SoCall, so no accuracy is claimed. Power is gross module input over each process run, including setup and warm-up, with an uncalibrated INA3221 scale. One earlier attempt is excluded because its power log was not written.
SOCALL-010.output_check: Byte-identical FASTQ to SOCALL-004 in all three process runs (and in the excluded attempt).
SOCALL-010.timing: Timed processing passes with CUDA synchronization at stage boundaries; the GPU argmax is counted as decode time. Model and NPZ loading were excluded.

SOCALL-011.title: Jetson TX2 D5 Baseline with Reference Accuracy
SOCALL-011.objective: Run all 4,467 D5 reads (R9.4.1, 4 kHz, matching SoCall's training chemistry) on the TX2 GPU and score the output against the reference genome.
SOCALL-011.decode: argmax on the GPU, vectorised collapse, float64 quality math
SOCALL-011.observation: The TX2 processed D5 at 44% of the 4 kHz full-channel reference, including FAST5 reading. Accuracy matched the Apple M2 run (SOCALL-001) to 0.01 points of median identity with the same mapped fraction, so the embedded deployment reproduces the reference pipeline's accuracy. GPU utilisation was 86%, against 44% on the short D1 reads.
SOCALL-011.limitations: One timed pass on one board. Beam search was not run on the TX2. Power is gross module input over the whole capture with an uncalibrated INA3221 scale. 64 reads differ from SOCALL-001 mid-read by a few bases for an unverified reason.
SOCALL-011.output_check: 4,467 reads; scored on the Mac with reference_accuracy.py against the D5 reference.
SOCALL-011.timing: One timed pass over all reads after a 50-read warm-up, including FAST5 reading and pA conversion. Model load and read indexing were excluded.

SOCALL-012.title: Jetson TX2 Same-Session Control for BatchNorm Folding and FP16
SOCALL-012.objective: Rerun the unchanged FP32 model with the SOCALL-010 decoder as the control for the folding and FP16 variants measured in the same session.
SOCALL-012.decode: argmax on the GPU, vectorised collapse, float64 quality math
SOCALL-012.observation: Throughput matched SOCALL-010 (964,273 samples/s) to within 0.01%, and the FASTQ was byte-identical to SOCALL-004 and SOCALL-010, so the board behaved the same as in the previous session.
SOCALL-012.limitations: D1 is out of distribution for SoCall, so no accuracy is claimed here. Power is gross module input over each process run, including setup and warm-up, with an uncalibrated INA3221 scale.
SOCALL-012.output_check: Byte-identical FASTQ to SOCALL-004 and SOCALL-010 in all three process runs.
SOCALL-012.timing: Timed processing passes with CUDA synchronization at stage boundaries; each process run had one untimed warm-up pass and then timed passes for at least 60 s. Model loading, BatchNorm folding and NPZ loading were excluded.

SOCALL-013.title: Jetson TX2 BatchNorm Folded into the Convolutions (FP32)
SOCALL-013.objective: Measure SoCall with each BatchNorm folded into the convolution before it, which removes five normalization layers without changing the math.
SOCALL-013.decode: argmax on the GPU, vectorised collapse, float64 quality math
SOCALL-013.observation: Folding gave 1.034× the same-session control. All 59 D1 sequences were identical to the control; 7 reads had quality strings that moved by one Phred step, because folding changes the FP32 rounding of the probabilities slightly. It is a small exact gain, and the folded model is the base for the FP16 and TensorRT variants.
SOCALL-013.limitations: D1 is out of distribution for SoCall, so no accuracy is claimed here. Power is gross module input over each process run, including setup and warm-up, with an uncalibrated INA3221 scale. The fold is checked against the unfolded model on the CPU at load time (max abs log-prob difference under 1e-4).
SOCALL-013.output_check: Same sequences as SOCALL-012 on all 59 reads; quality strings identical on 52.
SOCALL-013.timing: Timed processing passes with CUDA synchronization at stage boundaries; each process run had one untimed warm-up pass and then timed passes for at least 60 s. Model loading, BatchNorm folding and NPZ loading were excluded.

SOCALL-014.title: Jetson TX2 FP16 Through PyTorch (Folded Model)
SOCALL-014.objective: Measure the folded model in half precision through PyTorch and cuDNN, the quickest way to get an FP16 number on the TX2.
SOCALL-014.decode: argmax on the GPU, vectorised collapse, float64 quality math
SOCALL-014.observation: FP16 was slower: 0.873× the control and 0.844× the folded FP32 model, even though GPU memory use halved (60 vs 112 MiB). The same model is 2.6× faster in FP16 on an Apple M2, so the slowdown is specific to how PyTorch 1.10 runs FP16 convolutions on this GPU. The likely cause, FP32 accumulation without the Pascal half2 rate, is not verified. TensorRT FP16 is measured separately.
SOCALL-014.limitations: D1 is out of distribution for SoCall, so no accuracy is claimed here. Power is gross module input over each process run, including setup and warm-up, with an uncalibrated INA3221 scale. Sequences differ from the control because FP16 rounding moves near-tied labels; accuracy is judged on D5 in SOCALL-016.
SOCALL-014.output_check: 0 of 59 sequences identical to SOCALL-012 (expected for FP16 on long reads); see SOCALL-016 for reference-scored accuracy.
SOCALL-014.timing: Timed processing passes with CUDA synchronization at stage boundaries; each process run had one untimed warm-up pass and then timed passes for at least 60 s. Model loading, BatchNorm folding and NPZ loading were excluded.

SOCALL-015.title: Jetson TX2 D5 with BatchNorm Folded (FP32)
SOCALL-015.objective: Run all 4,467 D5 reads with the folded FP32 model and check its accuracy against SOCALL-011.
SOCALL-015.decode: argmax on the GPU, vectorised collapse, float64 quality math
SOCALL-015.observation: Throughput was 1.043× SOCALL-011, including FAST5 reading. Median identity (79.39%) and mapped fraction (97.31%) were the same as SOCALL-011 to two decimals, and 4,392 of 4,467 reads were byte-identical. The other 75 reads differ where two labels were tied at FP32 resolution.
SOCALL-015.limitations: One timed pass on one board, greedy decoding only. Power is gross module input over the whole capture with an uncalibrated INA3221 scale. The run was in a later session than SOCALL-011, without a same-session D5 control.
SOCALL-015.output_check: 4,467 reads; scored on the Mac with reference_accuracy.py against the D5 reference and compared read by read with SOCALL-011.
SOCALL-015.timing: One timed pass over all reads after a 50-read warm-up, including FAST5 reading and pA conversion. Model loading, BatchNorm folding and read indexing were excluded.

SOCALL-016.title: Jetson TX2 D5 in FP16 Through PyTorch
SOCALL-016.objective: Check FP16 accuracy on the TX2's own GPU on all 4,467 D5 reads, against the project's FP16 budget of 0.1 points of median identity.
SOCALL-016.decode: argmax on the GPU, vectorised collapse, float64 quality math
SOCALL-016.observation: Median identity was 79.38% (0.010 points below SOCALL-011) and 97.38% of reads mapped (0.07 points above), so FP16 is within the accuracy budget on the TX2. Only 5 reads were byte-identical: FP16 moves many near-tied labels, but the changes cancel out in accuracy. Throughput was 0.854× the folded FP32 run, matching the D1 result.
SOCALL-016.limitations: One timed pass on one board, greedy decoding only. Power is gross module input over the whole capture with an uncalibrated INA3221 scale. FP16 through PyTorch is slower than FP32 here, so this run records accuracy rather than a speed option.
SOCALL-016.output_check: 4,467 reads; scored on the Mac with reference_accuracy.py against the D5 reference and compared read by read with SOCALL-011.
SOCALL-016.timing: One timed pass over all reads after a 50-read warm-up, including FAST5 reading and pA conversion. Model loading, BatchNorm folding and read indexing were excluded.
